feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-focused roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is slightly repetitive and could be tighter, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization show growth, trust, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good impact signals: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and analytics stack details add substance.  
- Strong positioning: headline, summary, and skills consistently support a digital strategy/communications leadership brand.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to save space and improve focus.  
- Add more outcome-driven results: several bullets describe responsibilities well but would be stronger with measurable business/communications outcomes (engagement growth, efficiency gains, campaign performance).  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); standardize serial comma usage (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “content operations and enterprise web improvement”); “front-end” and “organization-wide” are consistent, but punctuation/bullet formatting in job descriptions should be cleaned up for readability.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of seniority and more concise phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Add a clearer senior-level positioning tied to recent roles, e.g., “digital strategy leader” or “communications leader for mission-driven organizations.”
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a tighter grouping such as “multi-channel digital communications, web platforms, and content operations.”
- Consider rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel communications, web platforms, content operations, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, editorial workflows, and stakeholder coordination, with a strong track record translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible advocacy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely repeat Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” are also reinforced elsewhere, so keep the intro high-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is too broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, sharper phrasing and favor leadership-level terms: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS management • Editorial operations & governance • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow automation & systems design • Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional collaboration • Advocacy, policy & public-sector messaging • Multimedia, video & live event production
- Change “Multi-channel communication” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” for stronger grammar and seniority.
- Replace “Workflow & systems architecture” with “Workflow automation & systems design” unless you want to emphasize enterprise architecture specifically.
- Consider ordering by relevance/recency: strategy, platforms, operations, analytics, collaboration, advocacy, multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” repeats ideas already covered in the header and Soft Skills.
- This section substantially overlaps with Topline Skills; consider shortening one of the two.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and good alignment to your headline, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, named platforms, and 2–3 signature contributions so it feels distinct from your NACo leadership roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client context: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on enterprise web strategy, campaign delivery, and content operations for public-facing digital communications.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance: “Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved cross-team coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.” Add metrics if possible: number of sites, users, publishers, or time saved.
- Sharpen the AI bullet: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content modeling, and user-facing discovery.” If possible, add stage/result: prototype launched, search coverage improved, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps heavily with the NACo Director role; keep this item focused on consulting delivery and recent technical execution.
- The AI search and microsite bullets also repeat Recent Projects; avoid describing the same work in near-identical language.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a national association.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more measurable where possible: add team size, budget, % gains in traffic/engagement, reporting efficiency, production cost savings, or turnaround improvements from the studio/analytics buildout.
- Tighten softer bullets: replace “strengthened”/“improving” with concrete results, e.g., “Implemented publishing governance and cross-department planning systems that improved consistency and streamlined approvals.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program growth may duplicate earlier NACo bullets; emphasize building the in-house studio, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid mid-level progression item, but it reads generic and overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Emphasize executional leadership, channel ownership, and any concrete growth or cadence metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial and advocacy publishing across teams.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show ownership and outcome: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets and add measurable outcomes if available: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director role; keep this version more execution-focused, not strategic/governance-heavy.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; clarify this entry as scaling/formalizing the series rather than originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing like “audience-focused content planning.”

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive terms tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & publishing operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Content strategy for high-volume, mission-driven audiences
- Consider swapping “multi-channel communications leadership” for “cross-channel communications operations” only if you want consistency with Core Competencies.
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale-oriented language instead of soft phrasing: “10,000+ page ecosystems,” “50+ publishers,” or “high-volume public-sector communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already covered in the header/Core Competencies; keep only if this section needs sector specialization.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and reads as a tool dump rather than a senior, impact-oriented topline summary. For this section, emphasize modernization and execution themes over listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal and CMS modernization first; they align best with the most recent and highest-impact work.
- Trim generic platform listing where possible; “enterprise CMS modernization” is stronger than separate CMS names alone.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier: “for large public-facing, multi-publisher sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep this version strategic and let “Technical + IT” hold the full tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating it verbatim in multiple places if space is tight.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. Make it more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + tools: “Analytics strategy, KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, and insight generation using GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Consider tightening to 5–6 items max: “Analytics strategy • KPI design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO & performance analysis • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Use “executive reporting” instead of “leadership reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If you want more impact, add a light outcome cue: “decision-ready dashboards” or “measurement frameworks for web modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and reserve tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple work bullets. Make it tighter, more senior, and oriented to delivery capability rather than listing tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- PTZ camera and in-house studio operations  
- Virtual event workflows and technical delivery
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scale language such as “recurring advocacy programming” or “broadcast-quality in-house studio production” to reinforce impact.
- Consider dropping “editing” if Premiere Pro already appears in Technical + IT; keep this section focused on capability, not software.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlap with Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- “Studio operations” and production details are already evidenced in the Director of Digital Media role; avoid overloading this skills section with the same phrasing.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either be tighter and more senior-focused or add proficiency/context that supports recent Drupal-led work.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding light context: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, group by strength: **Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; avoid over-formatting or adding tools that belong under coding/automation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one instance or making this version more specific (e.g., “Platforms used” vs. “Technical strengths”).
- GitHub Pages may undersell seniority unless it supports a notable project; consider dropping it if space is tight.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. It should emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and signal current relevance.

Suggested edit
- Rename to something tighter and more modern, e.g. **Front-End & Technical Implementation**.
- Trim older/basic terms unless needed for ATS; consider: **JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • HTML/CSS**
- De-emphasize or remove **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in recent work; it can date the profile.
- If space allows, add specificity tied to recent work: **JavaScript for front-end implementation, CMS enhancements, tagging, serverless scripts, and deployment workflows**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- **Workflow automation** in Topline Skills may overlap with **GitHub Actions** here; keep one at high level and one tool-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to grouped, capability-led phrasing: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project/ops platforms: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant tools first; if Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier are the real differentiators, lead with those and consider dropping one or two lower-value PM tools.
- If accurate, add a light outcomes cue in the heading or nearby context, e.g. “used to streamline editorial planning, approvals, and cross-team communications workflows.”
- Consider renaming the category to “Workflow Automation & Operations Systems” to better match your senior-level positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Listing four PM tools (Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello) may feel redundant unless each reflects meaningful recent use.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare and undersells your email-platform leadership. It should signal enterprise-scale campaign/communications operations without repeating newsletter management already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/context rather than just names: **Enterprise email campaign platforms, newsletter operations, audience engagement and journey orchestration**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, order by recency/strength of use rather than alphabetically

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters” or audience-size claims here; those are already covered in the NACo roles
- “Engagement” is vague unless tied to journeys, segmentation, automation, or campaign operations

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it to emphasize foundational impact, team-building, and distinct early-career contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make contributions more concrete: replace “major website refresh” with scope or result if available (e.g., platform, traffic, usability, publishing efficiency).
- Clarify production ownership: “Produced livestreams and launched/managed recurring weekly video updates” reads stronger than “high-impact digital content.”
- Tighten management phrasing: “supervised and coached a digital media associate” is more direct than “provided day-to-day guidance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this item focused on launching/building the capability, and let the later role emphasize scaling it.
- “strengthening workflows” also appears in later NACo roles; here, frame it as early process-building rather than mature operations leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/program work plus the podcast launch.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer outcome-oriented line, e.g., “Produced multimedia and digital content that supported program visibility and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or results: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or programs/policy areas served.
- Keep it to 1–2 lines; this is an older role, so concise proof of progression is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia leadership already covered in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize general digital operations; save space for podcast launch and innovation/research coordination.
